
# How to Set Up and Use Your Roku


## What is this in plain English?


Think of Roku as a translator between the internet and your TV. Back in the 1980s and 90s, if you wanted to watch a movie, you drove to Blockbuster, rented a VHS tape, brought it home, and physically inserted it into your VCR. If you wanted to watch different content, you needed different physical devices: a VCR for rented movies, a cable box for TV channels, a game console for games, a CD player for music. Your entertainment center was a tangled mess of boxes, wires, and remote controls.


Roku is a small device—about the size of a deck of cards or a USB stick—that plugs into your TV and gives you access to thousands of "channels" (apps) that stream movies, TV shows, music, news, and more over the internet. Instead of driving to rent a movie, you browse Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon Prime and start watching instantly. Instead of flipping through 500 cable channels hoping something good is on, you search for exactly what you want to watch and play it immediately. Instead of needing separate devices for different services, Roku puts everything in one simple interface.


It's like the difference between a landline telephone directory (flip through pages to find a number) and a smartphone (type a name and instantly call). Roku takes all the entertainment available on the internet—streaming services, free content, music, news, sports—and makes it easily accessible through your TV with one simple remote control. You don't need to be tech-savvy, you don't need a computer science degree, and you don't need to understand how the internet works. You just need to know how to point a remote and click a button.


This guide will walk you through everything: choosing the right Roku device, connecting it to your TV, setting up your account, finding shows and movies, using the remote, troubleshooting problems, and getting the most from your Roku. By the end, you'll wonder how you ever lived without it.


## Before You Start: Understanding What Roku Is and What You Need


**What Exactly Is Roku?**


**Roku is a streaming device that:**

- Connects to your TV (via HDMI cable)
- Connects to your internet (via WiFi or Ethernet)
- Gives you access to streaming services (Netflix, Hulu, YouTube, etc.)
- Provides one simple interface for all your content
- Works with one remote control

**Think of it as a cable box replacement that uses the internet instead of cable.**


**What Roku Is NOT:**

- ❌ Not a monthly subscription service (the device is one-time purchase)
- ❌ Not a replacement for internet (you still need home internet)
- ❌ Not free content (though free channels exist, most require subscriptions)
- ❌ Not a DVR (can't record live TV, though some services offer cloud DVR)
- ❌ Not required if you have a Smart TV (but often better than built-in Smart TV features)

**Why Use Roku Instead of Smart TV Built-In Apps?**


**Advantages of Roku:**

- ✓ Faster and smoother than most Smart TV interfaces
- ✓ More frequent updates (better long-term support)
- ✓ More apps/channels available (3,000+ vs Smart TV's limited selection)
- ✓ Easier to replace when outdated ($30-50 vs $500+ TV)
- ✓ Universal search across all services
- ✓ Consistent interface (doesn't change when you buy new TV)
- ✓ Works with any TV (even old "dumb" TVs from 2010)

**Many people with Smart TVs still add Roku because it's better.**


**Types of Roku Devices:**


**Roku Express ($30):**

- **Best for:** Beginners, budget-conscious, HD TVs
- **Streams:** HD (1080p)
- **WiFi:** 2.4 GHz only
- **Remote:** Standard infrared (IR) remote
- **Pros:** Cheapest option, perfectly functional
- **Cons:** No 4K, basic remote, slower WiFi

**Roku Express 4K / Express 4K+ ($40):**

- **Best for:** 4K TV owners on budget
- **Streams:** 4K, HDR, HD
- **WiFi:** Dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz)
- **Remote:** Voice remote
- **Pros:** 4K support, better WiFi, voice search
- **Cons:** Still entry-level performance

**Roku Streaming Stick 4K ($50):**

- **Best for:** Most people, best value
- **Streams:** 4K, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HD
- **WiFi:** Long-range dual-band WiFi
- **Remote:** Voice remote with TV controls
- **Form factor:** USB stick (plugs directly into TV, no cable)
- **Pros:** Excellent performance, hidden behind TV, great remote
- **Cons:** None really—sweet spot for most users

**Roku Ultra ($100):**

- **Best for:** Power users, large homes, Ethernet connection desired
- **Streams:** 4K, all HDR formats
- **WiFi:** Excellent dual-band WiFi
- **Ethernet:** Wired connection option (more reliable)
- **Remote:** Premium voice remote with rechargeable battery, headphone jack (private listening), programmable buttons
- **Pros:** Fastest performance, most features, best remote, Ethernet port
- **Cons:** Most expensive, larger device (not as discreet)

**Roku Streambar ($130):**

- **Best for:** Those wanting better TV sound + streaming
- **What it is:** Soundbar + Roku in one device
- **Streams:** 4K HDR
- **Sound:** Improved over TV speakers
- **Pros:** Two devices in one, better audio
- **Cons:** Soundbar not as good as dedicated soundbar

**Roku TV (varies, $150-800):**

- **What it is:** TV with Roku built-in (TCL, Hisense brands primarily)
- **Best for:** Buying new TV anyway
- **Pros:** No separate device needed, seamless integration
- **Cons:** When Roku becomes outdated, whole TV feels slow (can add external Roku then)

**Our Recommendation for Most People:**


**Roku Streaming Stick 4K ($50)**

- Perfect balance of features and price
- 4K support (future-proof)
- Voice remote included
- Small and discreet
- Excellent performance

**Or Roku Express ($30) if:**

- You have HD TV (not 4K)
- Tight budget
- Basic needs (just Netflix and YouTube)

**What You Need to Use Roku:**


**Essential:**

1. **Roku device** (purchased separately)
2. **TV with HDMI port** (any TV from 2010+)
3. **Internet connection** (home WiFi or Ethernet)
    - Minimum speed: 3 Mbps (for SD quality)
    - Recommended: 25 Mbps for HD, 50+ Mbps for 4K
4. **WiFi password** (to connect Roku to internet)
5. **Power outlet** (to plug in Roku power adapter)
6. **Email address** (to create Roku account)
7. **Payment method** (credit/debit card for Roku account, even for free content)

**Helpful but optional:**
8. **Smartphone** (makes setup easier, can be used as remote)
9. **Streaming service subscriptions** (Netflix, Hulu, etc.)
10. **TV antenna** (for free local channels, if Roku model supports)


**Note: Roku doesn't require monthly subscription, but the content you want to watch usually does.**


**Understanding the Roku Account:**


**You must create a Roku account (free) to use any Roku device.**


**Account includes:**

- Email address
- Password
- Payment method (credit card or PayPal)
- Linked Roku devices
- Channel/app subscriptions
- Purchase history

**Why payment method is required even for free content:**

- Allows one-click purchases/rentals
- Subscribing to services through Roku
- Some "free trials" require card on file
- **You won't be charged unless you explicitly purchase something**

**Can use prepaid Visa gift card if you don't want to use real credit card**


**What Streaming Services Cost:**


**Roku is free. Content usually isn't.**


**Popular paid services (monthly subscriptions):**

- Netflix: $7-23/month
- Hulu: $8-18/month
- Disney+: $8-14/month
- HBO Max/Max: $10-20/month
- Amazon Prime Video: $9/month (or $139/year with Prime)
- Apple TV+: $7/month
- Paramount+: $6-12/month
- Peacock: Free-$12/month
- YouTube TV: $73/month (live TV)
- Sling TV: $40-55/month (live TV)

**Popular free services (with ads):**

- The Roku Channel (free movies, shows, live TV)
- Pluto TV (free live channels)
- Tubi (free movies and shows)
- YouTube (free videos)
- Crackle (free movies)
- Freevee (Amazon's free service)
- Local news apps
- Many more (500+ free channels on Roku)

**You don't need paid services to use Roku—plenty of free content available.**


**Internet Requirements:**


**Streaming uses internet data. How much you need:**


**Speed requirements:**

- 3 Mbps: SD quality (480p) - acceptable
- 5 Mbps: HD quality (720p) - good
- 25 Mbps: Full HD (1080p) - great
- 50+ Mbps: 4K/Ultra HD - best

**For households with multiple users:**

- Add 25 Mbps per 4K stream
- Example: 2 people streaming 4K + web browsing = need 100+ Mbps

**Data usage (if you have data cap):**

- SD: 1 GB per hour
- HD: 3 GB per hour
- 4K: 7 GB per hour

**Monthly estimate:**

- 2 hours daily in HD = 180 GB/month
- 4 hours daily in HD = 360 GB/month

**Most US internet plans:** Unlimited or 1TB+ cap (sufficient for streaming)


**Check your internet speed:**

- Visit speedtest.net on computer or phone
- Run test
- If speeds lower than needed, contact internet provider about upgrading

**What's In The Box:**


**When you purchase Roku device, you get:**


**All models include:**

- Roku device (stick or box)
- Remote control (with batteries usually)
- Power cable and adapter
- HDMI cable (Roku Express) OR built-into stick (Streaming Stick)
- Quick start guide

**Roku Ultra additionally includes:**

- Ethernet cable
- Premium remote with rechargeable battery
- Remote finder button (device beeps when you press button on Roku)
- USB port (for playing local media)

**What's NOT included:**

- ❌ HDMI cable (on some models—Streaming Stick doesn't need one)
- ❌ Streaming service subscriptions
- ❌ Roku account (create free during setup)

**Timeline Expectations:**


**Setup time:** 15-30 minutes
**Learning curve:** 1-2 days to feel comfortable
**Mastery:** 1 week of regular use


**By week two, navigating Roku will feel effortless.**


**The "Cord-Cutting" Decision:** Many people buy Roku specifically to "cut the cord"—cancel expensive cable TV and switch to streaming. This can save $50-150 per month. However, be aware that if you subscribe to multiple streaming services, costs add up quickly. Most cord-cutters save money by choosing 2-3 services they actually watch, rotating subscriptions seasonally (subscribe to HBO for two months to watch a show, cancel, subscribe to Disney+ for two months, etc.). Roku makes this easy since there's no contract—subscribe and cancel anytime.


## Step 1: Unboxing and Physical Setup


Let's get your Roku device physically connected to your TV.


**Unboxing Your Roku:**


**Step 1: Open the box carefully**

- Remove all contents
- Check you have all pieces (device, remote, cables, power adapter)
- **Keep the box for 30 days** (in case you need to return)

**Step 2: Remove any protective film**

- Peel plastic film off Roku device
- Remove battery tab from remote (makes batteries active)

**Step 3: Identify your cables**


**Roku Express/Express 4K:**

- **HDMI cable** (black cable with trapezoid-shaped ends)
- **Power cable** (micro-USB to wall adapter)

**Roku Streaming Stick:**

- **No HDMI cable needed** (built into stick)
- **Power cable** (micro-USB or USB-C to wall adapter)
- **Optional HDMI extender** (short cable to move stick away from TV)

**Roku Ultra:**

- **HDMI cable**
- **Power cable** (standard AC adapter)
- **Ethernet cable** (optional, for wired connection)

**Connecting Roku to Your TV:**


**Step 1: Locate HDMI port on your TV**

1. **Look at back or side of TV**
2. **Find HDMI ports** (usually multiple ports labeled HDMI 1, HDMI 2, HDMI 3, etc.)
3. **Choose any available HDMI port**
    - Ideally one that's easily accessible
    - Note which number (you'll need this to select input)
4. **If all HDMI ports occupied:** Disconnect device you use least, or buy HDMI switch ($15-25 on Amazon)

**HDMI ports look like:** Small rectangular port, slightly wider on bottom, with trapezoid shape


**Step 2: Connect Roku to HDMI port**


**For Roku Express/Express 4K/Ultra (box-style devices):**

1. **Take HDMI cable**
2. **Plug one end into HDMI port on TV** (push gently until fully seated)
3. **Plug other end into HDMI port on Roku device**
4. **Connection made**

**For Roku Streaming Stick:**

1. **Plug Roku stick directly into TV's HDMI port**
2. **Push gently until fully inserted**
3. **If stick doesn't fit easily** (blocked by other cables or TV frame):
    - Use included HDMI extender cable
    - Connect extender to TV's HDMI port
    - Connect Roku stick to extender
    - Gives more clearance

**Step 3: Connect power**


**All Roku devices need power:**


**Roku Express/Streaming Stick (USB powered):**


**Option A: Power from TV's USB port (if available)**

1. **Look for USB port on TV** (usually near HDMI ports)
2. **Plug Roku's micro-USB cable into TV's USB port**
3. **Plug other end into Roku device**
4. **Benefit:** One less cable to wall outlet, Roku turns on/off with TV
5. **Downside:** Some TV USB ports don't provide enough power (Roku will display warning)

**Option B: Power from wall outlet (most reliable)**

1. **Plug micro-USB cable into Roku device**
2. **Plug USB cable into included power adapter**
3. **Plug power adapter into wall outlet**
4. **Always provides sufficient power** (use this if Option A doesn't work)

**Roku Ultra (AC powered):**

1. **Plug power cord into back of Roku Ultra**
2. **Plug other end into wall outlet**
3. **No USB power option**—must use wall outlet

**Step 4: Organize cables neatly**

- Route cables behind TV stand or along wall
- Use cable ties or clips if desired
- Keep cables from being too tight (strain on connections)

**Positioning Roku Device:**


**For box-style Rokus (Express, Ultra):**

- **Place on TV stand** near TV
- **Ensure good ventilation** (don't stack other devices on top)
- **Keep in line of sight** if using IR remote (Express)
- **Can hide in cabinet** if using WiFi remote (Express 4K+, Stick, Ultra)

**For Roku Streaming Stick:**

- **Plugged into TV, hangs behind TV**
- **Nearly invisible**
- **Ensure good WiFi reception** (far side of TV from router may have weaker signal)
- **Use HDMI extender** if needed to improve WiFi reception

**Step 5: Turn on TV**

1. **Press power button** on TV remote
2. **TV turns on**
3. **Roku automatically turns on** when TV is on (if powered by TV USB) or when plugged into wall

**Step 6: Select correct HDMI input**


**Your TV needs to "see" the Roku:**

1. **Press "Input," "Source," or "HDMI" button** on TV remote
2. **See list of inputs:** HDMI 1, HDMI 2, HDMI 3, etc.
3. **Highlight the HDMI port** where you plugged in Roku
    - Example: If you used HDMI 2, select HDMI 2
4. **Press OK or Enter**
5. **TV switches to that input**

**You should now see Roku logo or welcome screen**


**If you see "No Signal" or blank screen:**

- Double-check HDMI cable is firmly connected (both ends)
- Try different HDMI port on TV
- Make sure Roku has power (light on device)
- Try different HDMI cable if available

**Setting Up the Remote:**


**Roku remotes come in two types:**


**IR (Infrared) Remote - Roku Express:**

- **Requires line of sight** to Roku device
- **Point directly at Roku** when pressing buttons
- **Batteries:** Usually 2 AA or 2 AAA (included)
- **No pairing needed**—works immediately

**WiFi/RF Remote - Express 4K+, Streaming Stick, Ultra:**

- **No line of sight needed** (works through walls, cabinets)
- **Connects via WiFi** to Roku
- **Batteries:** 2 AA (included)
- **Auto-pairs during setup** (usually)

**If remote doesn't work:**


**Check batteries:**

1. **Open battery compartment** (on back of remote)
2. **Check batteries are inserted correctly** (+ and - symbols)
3. **Replace batteries** if needed (old batteries may not work)

**For WiFi remotes - Manual pairing:**

1. **Remove batteries from remote**
2. **Unplug Roku device** (power)
3. **Wait 5 seconds**
4. **Plug Roku back in**
5. **Wait for Roku home screen to appear**
6. **Reinsert batteries in remote**
7. **Pairing light flashes on remote** (or press pairing button if present)
8. **Wait 30 seconds** for pairing
9. **Remote should work**

**Understanding the Remote Buttons:**


**Essential buttons (all Roku remotes):**

- **Power button (⏻):** Turns TV on/off (if remote supports TV control)
- **Home button (🏠):** Returns to Roku home screen from anywhere
- **Back button (←):** Goes back one screen
- **OK/Select (center of directional pad):** Confirms selection
- **Directional pad (↑↓←→):** Navigate menus
- **Star button (✱ or Options):** Opens options menu for current screen
- **Rewind (⏪):** Jump backward in video
- **Play/Pause (▷/⏸):** Start/stop video
- **Fast Forward (⏩):** Skip forward in video

**Additional buttons (some remotes):**

- **Voice button (🎤 or magnifying glass):** Hold to speak search
- **Volume +/- buttons:** Adjust TV volume (if remote supports TV control)
- **Mute button:** Silence TV
- **Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Apple TV+ buttons:** Launch apps directly (varies by remote)

**Roku remotes are simple—just a few buttons for most functions.**


**Testing the Setup:**


**At this point, you should see:**

- Roku logo on TV screen
- Or Roku welcome screen
- Or setup wizard

**If yes: Success! Proceed to Step 2 (Setup Wizard)**


**If no:**


**Troubleshooting:**


**Black screen / No Signal:**

- Verify HDMI cable connected at both ends
- Try different HDMI input on TV
- Make sure TV is on correct input (try all HDMI options)
- Check Roku has power (status light on device)

**Roku logo appears then disappears:**

- Wait 2-3 minutes (initial boot takes time)
- If still blank, unplug Roku, wait 10 seconds, plug back in

**"No HDMI signal detected":**

- Try different HDMI cable
- Plug Roku into different HDMI port
- Restart TV and Roku

**Remote not working:**

- Check batteries installed correctly
- For IR remote: Point directly at Roku device
- For WiFi remote: Try pairing process above
- Test with Roku smartphone app as remote (temporary solution)

**HDMI Port Confusion:** If you're having trouble getting Roku to display on your TV, the most common issue is selecting the wrong HDMI input. Your TV might have 4 HDMI ports (HDMI 1, 2, 3, 4), and you need to select the exact one where Roku is plugged in. Press the "Input" or "Source" button on your TV remote repeatedly, cycling through each option until you see the Roku screen. Once you find it, you can rename that input to "Roku" in your TV settings for easier identification later.


## Step 2: Initial Setup and Creating Your Roku Account


Now that Roku is connected, let's go through the setup wizard and create your account.


**The Setup Wizard:**


**When Roku powers on for the first time, you'll see a setup wizard. Follow it step-by-step:**


**Step 1: Choose your language**

1. **Setup screen appears:** "Let's get started"
2. **Language selection** shows (English, Español, Français)
3. **Highlight your language** using arrow buttons on remote
4. **Press OK**

**Step 2: Set up your Roku device**


**Option A: Standard Setup (most people)**

1. **Select "Set up for home use"**
2. **Press OK**
3. **Continues to network setup**

**Option B: Retail/Store Mode**

- Only for stores displaying Roku
- **Don't select this** for home use

**Step 3: Connect to the internet**


**This is critical—Roku needs internet to function.**


**Choose connection type:**


**Wireless (WiFi) - Most Common:**

1. **Select "Wireless"**
2. **Roku scans for WiFi networks** (takes 10-20 seconds)
3. **List of networks appears:**
    - Your network name (SSID)
    - Neighbors' networks
    - Signal strength indicators (more bars = stronger)
4. **Highlight your WiFi network**
5. **Press OK**
6. **Enter WiFi password:**
    - On-screen keyboard appears
    - Use arrow keys to highlight each letter/number
    - Press OK to select
    - **Case-sensitive** (CAPITAL vs lowercase matters)
    - **Include all symbols** exactly as they appear
    - **Common mistakes:** Confusing 0 (zero) with O (letter), 1 (one) with I (letter)
    - **Backspace key** to delete mistakes
7. **Select "Connect"**
8. **Roku tests connection** (15-30 seconds)
9. **"Success" message** when connected

**Wired (Ethernet) - Roku Ultra Only:**

1. **Connect Ethernet cable:**
    - One end to Roku Ultra
    - Other end to router
2. **Select "Wired"** in setup
3. **Automatic connection** (no password needed)
4. **More reliable** than WiFi

**Tips for entering WiFi password:**

- **WiFi password usually on router** (sticker on bottom/back)
- Or in router paperwork
- Or ask whoever set up internet
- **Take your time**—accuracy more important than speed
- **Double-check before submitting**

**Troubleshooting WiFi connection:**


**"Can't find network":**

- Check router is on (lights should be active)
- Move Roku closer to router (temporarily, for setup)
- Restart router (unplug 30 seconds, plug back in, wait 2 minutes)
- Check if router broadcasts 2.4 GHz (some Rokus don't see 5 GHz only networks)

**"Wrong password":**

- Triple-check password (every character matters)
- Verify caps/lowercase
- Check for symbols
- Try entering in phone notes first, verify it looks right

**"Weak signal":**

- Move router higher (on shelf, not floor)
- Reduce obstacles between router and Roku
- Consider WiFi extender
- Use Ethernet if available (Roku Ultra)

**Step 4: Wait for software update**


**After connecting to internet:**

1. **Roku checks for software updates** automatically
2. **"Checking for updates..."** message appears
3. **If update available:**
    - **"Downloading update..."** shows progress bar
    - **Takes 5-15 minutes** depending on update size
    - **Roku restarts automatically**
    - **DON'T unplug during update** (can damage device)
4. **If no update needed:**
    - Proceeds to next step

**This ensures you have latest features and bug fixes.**


**Step 5: Activate your Roku**


**Now you need to link Roku device to a Roku account:**


**Roku displays activation screen:**

- **Shows activation code** (example: ABC123 or A1B2C3)
- **Shows URL:** roku.com/link
- **Leaves this screen visible** while you complete activation on another device

**On computer, tablet, or smartphone:**

1. **Open web browser** (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, etc.)
2. **Go to roku.com/link**
3. **See "Link your Roku device" page**
4. **Enter the activation code** shown on your TV
5. **Click "Submit"**

**Now you'll either sign in or create a Roku account:**


**Creating a New Roku Account:**

1. **Click "Create account"** (if you don't have one)
2. **Enter information:**
    - **First name**
    - **Last name**
    - **Email address** (must be valid—you'll verify it)
    - **Password** (create strong password)
        - At least 8 characters
        - Mix of letters, numbers, symbols
        - Example: Roku2024Stream!
    - **Re-enter password** (confirm)
3. **Click "Continue"**
4. **Check your email:**
    - Roku sends verification email
    - **Open email**
    - **Click verification link**
    - Confirms your email address
5. **Return to roku.com/link page**

**Adding Payment Method:**


**Roku requires payment method** (even though account is free):


**Why payment is required:**

- Enables one-click purchases/rentals
- Allows subscribing to services through Roku
- Some "free trials" need card on file
- **You won't be charged unless you buy something**

**Add payment:**

1. **Choose payment type:**
    - **Credit/Debit Card** (Visa, MasterCard, Amex, Discover)
    - **PayPal**
    - **Roku gift card** (if you have one)
2. **For Credit/Debit Card:**
    - **Card number** (16 digits)
    - **Expiration date** (MM/YY)
    - **Security code** (CVV—3 digits on back, or 4 on front for Amex)
    - **Billing zip code**
    - **Name on card**
3. **For PayPal:**
    - **Log in to PayPal**
    - **Authorize Roku** to use PayPal for payments
4. **Click "Submit"** or **"Continue"**

**If you don't want to use real credit card:**

- **Buy Visa/MasterCard gift card** ($25-50 at grocery/drug stores)
- **Use gift card as payment method**
- Can't be charged more than gift card balance

**Account creation complete!**

1. **Back on TV:** Roku receives activation confirmation
2. **Displays "Success!" or "You're all set!"**
3. **Roku restarts** (automatically)
4. **Shows home screen** in 30-60 seconds

**If Signing In to Existing Account:**

1. **Click "Sign In"** (instead of Create Account)
2. **Enter email and password** from existing Roku account
3. **Click "Sign In"**
4. **Verify payment method** on file
5. **Confirm linking** this Roku device to your account
6. **TV shows activation success**

**Step 6: Customize settings (optional)**


**Some Roku models ask preference questions:**


**Display type:**

- **Auto-detect (recommended):** Roku determines TV capabilities
- **HDTV:** 1080p HD
- **4K UHD TV:** 4K resolution
- **Usually auto-detect works perfectly**

**Connection:**

- Confirms WiFi or Ethernet
- Shows connection strength

**Roku completes setup:**

- **"You're all set!"** message
- **Shows home screen**

**Congratulations! Roku is now set up and ready to use.**


**Post-Setup Checklist:**


**Verify everything works:**

- [ ] Roku home screen appears
- [ ] Remote controls navigation (arrow keys move, OK selects)
- [ ] Internet connected (shows WiFi icon or signal strength)
- [ ] Account created and activated

**Before proceeding, make sure all above are working.**


**What Your Roku Home Screen Shows:**


**On first boot, you'll see:**


**Top of screen:**

- Search icon (magnifying glass)
- Settings icon (gear)
- Your account name

**Main area:**

- **Featured content** (banner ads and recommendations)
- **Channel grid** (empty at first, or with pre-installed channels)
    - Home
    - Search
    - Streaming Channels (app store)
    - Settings
    - The Roku Channel (free content)
    - Sometimes: Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Prime Video, YouTube (pre-installed)

**Bottom:**

- Tips or announcements (first time)

**Unfortunately, banner ads are permanent** (Roku's business model, how they keep device prices low)


**Next step: Adding channels/apps (Step 3)**


**Important Account Information to Remember:**


**Write down and store safely:**


`Roku Account Information:
Email: _______________________
Password: _____________________
Payment Method: ______________
Activation Date: ______________`


**You'll need this for:**

- Logging in on roku.com (to manage account)
- Adding channels from computer
- Managing subscriptions
- Troubleshooting with support

**Roku Account Management (roku.com):**


**What you can do on Roku website:**

- View linked devices
- Manage payment methods
- Update account information
- View purchase history
- Add channels remotely (appear on your Roku automatically)
- Manage subscriptions
- Set up PIN for purchases

**Access anytime at roku.com → Sign In**


**The Payment Method Requirement:** Many people get frustrated that Roku requires a credit card even to access free content. This is Roku's policy and cannot be bypassed (except with gift cards). Think of it like Amazon—you have a payment method on file, but you're only charged when you actually buy something. Roku won't charge you for activating the device, installing free channels, or watching free content. The card is only charged if you rent a movie, subscribe to a service through Roku, or make other explicit purchases. If you're still uncomfortable, use a prepaid Visa gift card with a small balance.


## Step 3: Adding Channels (Apps) and Organizing Your Home Screen


Roku calls apps "channels." Let's add the content you want to watch.


**Understanding Channels:**


**What are channels?**

- Roku's name for apps
- Each streaming service has a channel (Netflix channel, YouTube channel, etc.)
- Free and paid options
- 3,000+ channels available

**Types of channels:**


**Subscription channels:**

- Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, HBO Max, etc.
- Require monthly subscription (paid outside Roku or through Roku)
- Install channel free, pay for subscription separately

**Free channels (with ads):**

- The Roku Channel, Pluto TV, Tubi, YouTube, etc.
- Completely free, ad-supported
- No subscription needed

**Rental/Purchase channels:**

- Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Vudu, Google Play
- Rent movies ($3-6) or buy ($10-20)
- Pay per title

**Live TV channels:**

- YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, Sling TV
- Replace cable with streaming
- Monthly subscription

**Accessing the Roku Channel Store:**


**Step 1: From Roku home screen**

1. **Navigate to "Streaming Channels"** using arrow keys
    - Usually on left side or in main grid
    - Icon looks like magnifying glass or purple tile with "+"
2. **Press OK**
3. **Channel Store opens**

**Step 2: Browse channel store**


**You can browse by:**


**Categories:**

- **Featured:** Highlighted channels
- **Movies & TV:** Streaming services, movie apps
- **News & Weather:** CNN, Fox News, Weather Channel, local news
- **Sports:** ESPN, MLB, NBA, etc.
- **Kids & Family:** PBS Kids, Noggin, etc.
- **Music:** Spotify, Pandora, iHeart Radio
- **International:** Channels in other languages
- **And many more**

**Sections:**

- **What's New:** Recently added channels
- **Top Free:** Most popular free channels
- **Most Popular:** Overall most-used channels
- **My Channels:** Channels you've already added

**Step 3: Search for specific channel**

1. **In Channel Store, find Search**
2. **Type channel name** (example: "Netflix")
3. **Results appear**
4. **Select channel you want**

**Adding a Channel:**


**Example: Adding Netflix**

1. **Navigate to "Streaming Channels"**
2. **Search or browse for "Netflix"**
3. **Highlight Netflix**
4. **Press OK**
5. **Channel details page appears:**
    - Description
    - Screenshots
    - Rating
    - "Add Channel" button
6. **Select "Add Channel"**
7. **Press OK**
8. **Channel downloads** (takes 5-15 seconds)
9. **"Channel added" confirmation**
10. **Options appear:**
    - "Go to channel" (opens Netflix immediately)
    - "OK" (returns to channel store)

**Repeat for each channel you want to add.**


**Popular Channels to Add:**


**Most people add these:**


**Free channels:**

- The Roku Channel (free movies, shows, live TV)
- Pluto TV (free live TV channels)
- Tubi (free movies and shows)
- YouTube (free videos)
- PBS (free documentaries and shows)
- Local news apps (ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX)

**Paid subscriptions (if you have them):**

- Netflix
- Hulu
- Disney+
- HBO Max / Max
- Amazon Prime Video
- Apple TV+
- Paramount+
- Peacock
- ESPN+
- Discovery+

**You don't need to add every channel—just ones you'll actually use.**


**Start with 5-10 channels, add more later as needed.**


**Signing Into Channels:**


**After adding a channel, you need to sign in (for subscription services):**


**Example: Signing into Netflix**

1. **Open Netflix channel** (from home screen)
2. **Netflix welcome screen appears**
3. **Two options:**

**Option A: Sign in on TV**

1. **Select "Sign In"**
2. **Enter email** using on-screen keyboard
3. **Enter password**
4. **Sign in**
5. **Choose profile** (if you have multiple Netflix profiles)
6. **Start watching**

**Option B: Activate on another device (easier)**

1. **Select "Use a phone or computer to sign in"** or similar
2. **Netflix shows activation code** (example: ABCD1234)
3. **On phone/computer:** Go to netflix.com/activate
4. **Enter code from TV**
5. **Sign in** on phone/computer
6. **TV automatically signs in**

**Option B is much faster** (no typing with remote)


**Most channels use same activation pattern:**

- Display code on TV
- Visit activation URL on phone/computer
- Enter code
- Sign in on phone
- TV signs in automatically

**Free channels usually don't require sign-in** (just open and use)


**Organizing Your Home Screen:**


**Roku lets you rearrange channels on home screen:**


**How to move channels:**

1. **Highlight channel** you want to move
2. **Press ✱ (Star/Options) button** on remote
3. **Select "Move channel"**
4. **Use arrow keys** to reposition
    - Move up/down/left/right
5. **Press OK** when in desired location
6. **Channel moves to new spot**

**Organize by frequency of use:**

- **Most-used channels first** (Netflix, YouTube, etc.)
- **Rarely-used channels last**
- **Group similar channels** (all video channels together, music channels together)

**Removing Channels:**


**If you don't use a channel:**

1. **Highlight channel**
2. **Press ✱ (Star/Options)**
3. **Select "Remove channel"**
4. **Confirm removal**
5. **Channel deleted from home screen**

**Can always re-add later** from Channel Store


**Managing Subscriptions:**


**Subscriptions through Roku:**


**If you subscribed to service through Roku** (not separately):

- Charged through Roku account
- Billed to payment method on file
- Manage at roku.com → My Account → Manage Subscriptions

**How to cancel Roku subscriptions:**

1. Go to roku.com
2. Sign in
3. **My Account → Manage Subscriptions**
4. **Find subscription**
5. **Cancel subscription**
6. **Confirm**
7. **Access until end of billing period, then stops**

**Subscriptions through service directly:**


**If you subscribed on Netflix.com, Hulu.com, etc.** (not through Roku):

- Manage on that service's website
- Roku doesn't control it
- Change payment, cancel, etc. on their site

**Adding Channels from Computer:**


**You can add channels remotely:**

1. **On computer, go to channelstore.roku.com**
2. **Sign in** to your Roku account
3. **Browse channels**
4. **Click "Add Channel"** on any channel
5. **Channel automatically appears** on your Roku
    - May take a few minutes
    - Roku must be on and connected to internet

**Great for browsing and adding multiple channels quickly** (easier than using remote)


**Content Ratings and Parental Controls:**


**Setting up parental controls:**

1. **Home screen → Settings**
2. **Parental Controls**
3. **Create 4-digit PIN**
4. **Enable restrictions:**
    - Block content by rating (TV-MA, R, etc.)
    - Require PIN for purchases
    - Block adding/removing channels
5. **Save settings**

**Now rated content requires PIN to watch**


**Recommended settings for families:**

- Block TV-MA and R-rated content
- Require PIN for all purchases
- Require PIN to add channels

**The Roku Channel (Free Content):**


**Roku's own channel with free content:**


**What it includes:**

- **Free movies** (with ads)
- **Free TV shows** (with ads)
- **Live TV channels** (free news, sports, entertainment)
- **Premium subscriptions** (can subscribe to HBO, Showtime, etc. through Roku Channel)

**How to access:**

1. **Already installed** on Roku (pre-installed)
2. **Open "The Roku Channel"**
3. **Browse free content**
4. **No sign-in required** for free content
5. **Start watching**

**Surprisingly good selection** of free movies and shows


**Popular Free Channels Summary:**


**Movies and TV:**

- The Roku Channel
- Tubi
- Pluto TV
- Crackle

- YouTube

**Live TV:**

- Pluto TV (200+ live channels)
- The Roku Channel (live channels)
- Xumo
- Local Now (local news)

**News:**

- ABC News
- CBS News
- NBC News
- NewsON (local news stations)
- Haystack News

**Music:**

- YouTube
- Spotify (free with ads)
- Pandora
- iHeartRadio

**Kids:**

- PBS Kids
- YouTube Kids (if you enable it)
- Kidoodle TV

**Many, many more** (500+ free channels total)


**You can watch a lot without paying for subscriptions.**


**Channel Recommendations by Interest:**


**For movie lovers:**

- Netflix, Hulu, HBO Max, Disney+
- Tubi, The Roku Channel (free options)

**For TV show bingers:**

- Hulu (next-day TV)
- Netflix, HBO Max
- Paramount+ (CBS shows)

**For sports fans:**

- ESPN+
- FuboTV, YouTube TV (live sports)

**Channel Overwhelm:** With 3,000+ channels available, it's tempting to install everything. Resist this urge. Start with just the channels you know you'll use regularly. Too many channels makes it harder to find what you want. Most people are perfectly happy with 10-15 channels: Netflix, YouTube, Hulu, The Roku Channel, a few free movie channels, and maybe a music app. Install what you need, skip the rest. You can always add more later.


## Step 4: Finding and Watching Content


Now that you have channels installed, let's actually watch something!


**Navigating the Roku Home Screen:**


**Understanding what you see:**


**Home screen elements:**

- **Your channels** (grid of tiles showing installed channels)
- **Featured content** (banner at top showing recommended movies/shows)
- **Search** (magnifying glass icon)
- **Streaming Channels** (channel store)
- **Settings** (gear icon)

**Moving around home screen:**

1. **Use arrow keys** on remote
2. **Highlight different channels**
3. **Press OK** to open highlighted channel
4. **Press Home button** to return to home screen from anywhere

**Opening a Channel:**


**Example: Opening Netflix**

1. **From home screen, highlight Netflix**
2. **Press OK**
3. **Netflix opens** (takes 2-5 seconds to load)
4. **Netflix home screen appears**

**Each channel has its own interface** (different layouts, different navigation)


**Browsing Within a Channel:**


**Example: Browsing Netflix**


**What you see:**

- **Rows of content** (Trending Now, Popular on Netflix, Continue Watching, etc.)
- **Categories** (Action, Comedy, Documentaries, etc.)
- **Search** (find specific shows/movies)
- **Account icon** (profiles, settings, sign out)

**How to browse:**

1. **Use arrow keys** to navigate
2. **Scroll right/left** through rows
3. **Scroll up/down** between rows
4. **Highlight a show/movie** to see details

**Selecting Content to Watch:**


**When you highlight a show/movie:**


**Details appear:**

- Title
- Description
- Year, rating, runtime
- Cast and crew
- **Buttons:** Play, Add to My List, Rate, More Info

**To watch:**

1. **Press OK** while highlighting "Play" or the content itself
2. **Content starts playing** (may show ads first on free channels)
3. **Playback begins**

**Playback Controls:**


**While watching, you can:**


**Pause/Play:**

- **Press Play/Pause button** on remote
- Video pauses or resumes

**Rewind:**

- **Press ⏪ (Rewind) button**
- Jumps back 10 seconds (usually)
- Press repeatedly to jump back more

**Fast Forward:**

- **Press ⏩ (Fast Forward) button**
- Skips ahead 10 seconds
- Press repeatedly to skip more

**Scrub through video:**

- **Press OK** while playing
- **Progress bar appears**
- **Use left/right arrows** to move through video
- **See thumbnail preview** of that moment
- **Press OK** to jump to that point

**Exit playback:**

- **Press Back button** (←)
- Returns to channel/menu
- Or **Press Home button** to exit to Roku home screen

**Subtitles/Closed Captions:**


**Enabling subtitles:**


**While watching:**

1. **Press ✱ (Star/Options) button**
2. **Menu appears** with options
3. **Select "Captions" or "Subtitles"**
4. **Choose language:**
    - English
    - Spanish
    - Other languages (if available)
    - English [CC] (closed captions, includes sound descriptions)
5. **Subtitles appear** on screen

**To turn off:**

- Same process, select "Off"

**Subtitle options vary by channel and content**


**Using Roku Search:**


**Universal search is one of Roku's best features:**


**What Roku Search does:**

- **Searches across all your channels** at once
- Shows which services have the content
- Compares prices (rent/buy options)
- Tells you if content is free vs paid

**How to search:**


**Method 1: Voice Search (if your remote has microphone button)**

1. **Press and hold voice/microphone button** on remote
2. **Speak clearly:** "The Office" or "Tom Hanks movies" or "action movies"
3. **Release button**
4. **Roku processes voice**
5. **Search results appear**

**Method 2: Text Search**

1. **From home screen, go to Search**
2. **Press OK**
3. **On-screen keyboard appears**
4. **Type your search** using arrow keys
    - Show name
    - Movie title
    - Actor name
    - Director name
    - Genre
5. **Results appear as you type**
6. **Select result** you want

**Example search for "The Office":**


**Results show:**

- **Available on:** Netflix (Free with subscription), Peacock (Free with ads), Amazon Prime (Purchase $1.99/episode)
- **You can:** Select which service to watch on
- **Roku shows cheapest/free option first**

**This is incredibly powerful** - no need to open every app to see who has the show


**Searching by Category:**


**Voice search examples:**

- "Show me comedies"
- "Find documentaries"
- "Action movies"
- "Kids shows"

**Results show content** from all your channels in that category


**My Feed (Following Content):**


**"Follow" movies/shows not yet available:**

1. **Search for upcoming movie**
2. **Select "Follow"**
3. **Roku notifies you** when it becomes available for streaming
4. **Access "My Feed"** from home screen to see followed content

**Useful for:**

- Movies still in theaters
- Shows that haven't premiered yet
- Content you want to watch later

**Watching Live TV (If Available):**


**If you have:**

- Live TV streaming service (YouTube TV, Hulu Live, etc.)
- Antenna connected to Roku TV
- Live TV channels (Pluto TV, etc.)

**Accessing live TV:**


**For streaming services:**

1. **Open the channel** (YouTube TV, Hulu, etc.)
2. **Select "Live TV" or "Guide"**
3. **Browse channels**
4. **Select channel to watch**

**For free live channels (Pluto TV, Roku Channel):**

1. **Open channel**
2. **Select "Live TV"**
3. **Channel guide appears**
4. **Choose channel**
5. **Watch live**

**The Roku Channel has 100+ free live TV channels** (news, movies, entertainment)


**Resume Watching / Continue Watching:**


**Most channels remember where you stopped:**


**"Continue Watching" row:**

- Shows on home screen of each channel
- Lists shows/movies you started
- Select to resume where you left off
- Even if you stopped days ago

**This works:**

- Within each channel (Netflix remembers Netflix shows)
- Across devices (start on Roku, continue on phone app)

**Roku doesn't have universal Continue Watching** across all channels, but individual channels track your progress


**Adding to Watchlist / My List:**


**Save content to watch later:**


**In most channels:**

1. **Highlight show/movie**
2. **Press OK** to see details
3. **Select "+ My List" or "+ Watchlist"**
4. **Content saved**
5. **Access from "My List" section** in that channel

**Each channel has its own watchlist** (Netflix My List separate from Hulu watchlist, etc.)


**Ratings and Recommendations:**


**Improve recommendations:**


**Rate content:**

- Most channels show 👍 👎 or star ratings
- **Thumbs up:** Liked it
- **Thumbs down:** Didn't like it
- Helps channel recommend similar content

**The more you rate, the better recommendations become**


**Renting or Buying Movies:**


**For channels that offer rentals/purchases** (Amazon, Vudu, Apple TV):


**To rent a movie:**

1. **Search for movie** or **browse**
2. **Select movie**
3. **Choose "Rent" option**
    - SD or HD (HD costs more)
    - Typically $3-6
4. **Confirm purchase**
5. **Enter Roku PIN** (if PIN protection enabled)
6. **Movie added to library**
7. **Watch immediately** or within rental window (usually 30 days to start, 48 hours to finish once started)

**To buy a movie:**

- Same process
- Choose "Buy" instead of "Rent"
- Typically $10-20
- **Own forever** (in that service's library)
- **Watch anytime**

**Purchases billed to payment method on Roku account**


**Viewing Purchase History:**


**See what you've rented/bought:**

1. **Go to roku.com**
2. **Sign in**
3. **My Account → Purchase History**
4. **See all transactions**

**Also visible in individual channel's "My Library" or "Purchases" section**


**Watching on Multiple Roku Devices:**


**If you have multiple Rokus** (bedroom, living room, etc.):


**Same account on all:**

- Sign into same Roku account on each device
- Channels sync across devices
- Install channel once, appears on all Rokus

**Watch on different device:**

- Start show on living room Roku
- Continue on bedroom Roku
- Progress syncs (within each channel's service, not Roku itself)

**Simultaneous streams:**

- Depends on channel's rules
- Netflix: 2-4 streams depending on plan
- Hulu: 2 streams
- Disney+: 4 streams
- Each service has different limits

**Adjusting Playback Quality:**


**If buffering or poor quality:**


**Some channels let you adjust:**

1. **While playing, press ✱ (Star)**
2. **Look for "Quality" or "Video Settings"**
3. **Choose quality:**
    - Auto (recommended)
    - HD
    - SD
4. **Lower quality = less buffering** but worse picture

**Or adjust in Roku settings:**

- **Settings → Display Type**
- Change from 4K to 1080p if buffering on 4K content

**Tips for Finding Content:**


**Use Roku's "What to Watch" website:**

- whattowatch.roku.com
- Browse trending content
- See what's popular
- Filter by service
- Discover new shows/movies

**Check "Just Added" sections:**

- Each channel shows new arrivals
- Great for finding fresh content

**Explore genre categories:**

- Each channel has genres (Action, Comedy, Drama, etc.)
- Browse specific genre you're in the mood for

**Follow entertainment news:**

- Roku blog, streaming service announcements
- Reddit: r/Roku, r/NetflixBestOf, etc.
- Know when new content launches

**The Search Game-Changer:** Roku's universal search is the feature that justifies its existence. Instead of opening Netflix, searching, not finding the show, closing Netflix, opening Hulu, searching again, not finding it, opening Prime Video, searching again, etc.—you search once on Roku and it shows you everywhere that show is available and how much it costs. This saves massive amounts of time and frustration. Use voice search if your remote has it—saying "The Office" is so much faster than typing it letter-by-letter with the arrow keys.


## Step 5: Using the Roku Remote and Mobile App


Let's master the remote and explore the mobile app alternative.


**Understanding Your Roku Remote:**


**Button Reference:**


**Navigation:**

- **Directional Pad (↑↓←→):** Move cursor/highlight
- **OK/Select (center button):** Confirm choice
- **Back (←):** Go back one screen
- **Home (🏠):** Return to Roku home screen
- **✱ Star/Options:** Open options menu for current screen

**Playback:**

- **Play/Pause (▷/⏸):** Start or stop video
- **Rewind (⏪):** Jump backward (usually 10 sec)
- **Fast Forward (⏩):** Skip forward (usually 10 sec)

**Volume/Power (enhanced remotes):**

- **Power (⏻):** Turn TV on/off
- **Volume + / Volume -:** Adjust TV volume
- **Mute (🔇):** Silence TV

**Voice (enhanced remotes):**

- **Microphone button (🎤):** Hold to voice search/command

**Quick Launch:**

- **Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Apple TV+ buttons:** Launch apps directly
- **Varies by remote model**

**Roku Remote Types:**


**Standard IR Remote (Roku Express):**

- **Requires line of sight** to Roku
- **Must point at Roku** when pressing buttons
- **No voice search**
- **No TV controls** (volume, power)
- **Simple, functional**

**Enhanced Voice Remote (Express 4K+, Streaming Stick, Ultra):**

- **No line of sight needed** (works through walls)
- **Voice search** (microphone button)
- **TV controls** (power, volume, mute)
- **Headphone jack** (Ultra remote - private listening)
- **Rechargeable battery** (some Ultra models)

**Advanced Remote Features:**


**Voice Search and Commands:**


**How to use voice:**

1. **Press and hold microphone button**
2. **Speak clearly:**
    - "The Office"
    - "Tom Hanks movies"
    - "Romantic comedies"
    - "Launch Netflix"
    - "Play Stranger Things on Netflix"
3. **Release button**
4. **Roku processes and responds**

**What you can say:**

- **Search:** Any show, movie, actor, genre
- **Launch:** "Open Netflix," "Launch YouTube"
- **Control:** "Pause," "Play," "Rewind"
- **Questions:** "What's trending?" "What's new on Netflix?"

**Voice is much faster than typing**


**Programming Volume/Power Buttons:**


**If remote has TV controls but they don't work:**


**Setup TV control:**

1. **Settings → Remotes & devices → Remote**
2. **Set up remote for TV control**
3. **Choose your TV brand** from list
4. **Roku tests volume** (beeps or shows on TV)
5. **Confirm if working**
6. **Roku configures remote** for your TV

**Now power, volume, mute control your TV**


**If TV brand not listed:**

- Try "Other" or generic codes
- May require manual code entry (check Roku support site)

**Private Listening (Roku Mobile App or Ultra Remote with Headphone Jack):**


**Listen through headphones instead of TV speakers:**


**With Roku Ultra remote:**

1. **Plug headphones into remote's headphone jack**
2. **Audio automatically routes** to headphones
3. **TV mutes**
4. **Great for late-night watching** without disturbing others

**With Roku mobile app:**

- Covered in mobile app section below

**Lost Remote Finder (Roku Ultra):**


**Roku Ultra has built-in speaker:**


**To find lost remote:**

1. **Press button on Roku Ultra device** (labeled "Remote Finder")
2. **Remote beeps loudly**
3. **Follow sound to find remote**

**Extremely useful feature**


**Using the Roku Mobile App:**


**Download the app:**


**iOS (iPhone/iPad):**

1. **App Store**
2. **Search "Roku"**
3. **Download "The Roku App (Official)"** by Roku, Inc.
4. **Free**

**Android:**

1. **Google Play Store**
2. **Search "Roku"**
3. **Download "The Roku App (Official)"**
4. **Free**

**Setting Up the Mobile App:**

1. **Open Roku app**
2. **Sign in** with your Roku account (same email/password as roku.com)
3. **App finds Roku devices** on same WiFi network
4. **Select your Roku** from list
5. **Roku and app connect**

**Must be on same WiFi network** for app to work


**What the Mobile App Can Do:**


**Remote Control:**

- **Touchpad mode:** Swipe on phone to move cursor on TV
- **Touch keyboard:** Easy text entry (so much better than on-screen keyboard)
- **Voice search:** Speak into phone
- **Playback controls:** Play, pause, rewind, fast forward

**Private Listening:**

- **Plug headphones into phone**
- **Tap headphone icon in app**
- **TV audio plays through phone**
- **TV mutes**
- **Watch TV without disturbing others**

**Channels/Content:**

- **Browse channels** on phone
- **Launch channels** remotely
- **Add new channels** from app

**Casting:**

- **Cast photos from phone** to TV
- **Cast videos from phone** to TV
- **Cast music** to TV

**Using the App as Remote:**


**Touch Remote mode:**

1. **Open app**
2. **Tap "Remote" tab** at bottom
3. **Touchpad appears**
4. **Swipe to navigate** (like trackpad)
5. **Tap to select**
6. **Buttons at bottom:** Back, Home, Options, etc.

**Touch Keyboard mode:**

1. **When search or text entry needed**
2. **Keyboard automatically appears** on phone
3. **Type on phone keyboard** (normal typing)
4. **Text appears on TV**
5. **So much faster** than on-screen keyboard

**Voice search in app:**

1. **Tap microphone icon**
2. **Speak search term**
3. **Results appear on TV**

**Private Listening with App:**


**Step-by-step:**

1. **Plug headphones into phone** (or use Bluetooth headphones connected to phone)
2. **Open Roku app**
3. **Tap headphone icon** (in remote control screen)
4. **"Listening on [Your Phone]" appears**
5. **Audio now plays through phone/headphones**
6. **TV is muted**
7. **Continue watching TV** with private audio

**Adjust volume:**

- **Use phone's volume buttons**

**To stop private listening:**

- **Tap headphone icon again**
- **Audio returns to TV**

**Benefits:**

- Watch TV late at night without disturbing household
- Clearer audio (especially for dialogue)
- Multiple people can use private listening simultaneously (each with their own phone/headphones)

**Casting Photos/Videos from Phone:**


**Share your phone content on TV:**


**Photos:**

1. **In Roku app, tap "Photos" tab**
2. **Allow access to photos**
3. **Select photos** you want to show
4. **Photos display on TV**
5. **Swipe to change photos**

**Videos:**

1. **"Videos" or "Media" tab**
2. **Select video** from phone
3. **Plays on TV**

**Great for showing vacation photos to family on the big screen**


**Adding Channels from App:**

1. **In app, tap "Channels" tab**
2. **Browse channel store**
3. **Tap "Add Channel"** on any channel
4. **Channel automatically appears** on your Roku

**Easier than browsing on TV**


**Multiple Rokus in App:**


**If you have multiple Roku devices:**

1. **App lists all Rokus** on network
2. **Swipe to switch** between devices
3. **Control different Roku** in different room
4. **All from one app**

**Troubleshooting App Connection:**


**App can't find Roku:**

- **Check both phone and Roku on same WiFi network**
- **Restart Roku:** Settings → System → System Restart
- **Restart phone**
- **Reinstall app**

**App connected but not responding:**

- **Check WiFi signal strength**
- **Move closer to router**
- **Restart both devices**

**Using Physical Remote vs App:**


**When to use physical remote:**

- **Everyday browsing and watching**
- **More tactile, familiar**
- **Doesn't require phone battery**
- **Simpler for basic tasks**

**When to use app:**

- **Searching/typing** (much easier with phone keyboard)
- **Private listening** (without Roku Ultra)
- **Adding channels** (easier browsing)
- **Lost physical remote** (app is backup)
- **Showing photos/videos** from phone

**Many people use both:** Physical remote for most tasks, app for text entry and private listening


**Battery Tips for Physical Remote:**


**Extending battery life:**

- **Use rechargeable batteries** (AA or AAA)
- **Turn off remote** when not in use for extended periods (remove batteries)
- **Keep spare batteries** handy

**Roku remotes typically last 3-6 months** on batteries with regular use


**Enhanced remote battery indicators:**

- **Settings → Remotes & devices → Remote → About**
- **Shows battery level**

**The Mobile App Secret Weapon:** The Roku mobile app isn't just a nice-to-have—it's essential for anyone who values their sanity. Typing a search with the remote's on-screen keyboard is torture: press right arrow 17 times to get to "Q", press OK, press right 5 more times to get to "U", press OK... With the app, you just type normally on your phone. Additionally, private listening through the app is a game-changer for watching TV after everyone else has gone to bed. Download the app immediately, even if you think you won't use it. You will.


## Step 6: Customizing Settings for Better Experience


Let's optimize your Roku's settings for better picture, sound, and usability.


**Accessing Roku Settings:**


**From home screen:**

1. **Navigate to "Settings"** (gear icon)
2. **Press OK**
3. **Settings menu opens**

**Settings Categories:**


**Main settings sections:**

- Network
- Display type
- Audio
- Captions
- Screensaver
- Theme
- System
- Remotes & devices
- Privacy
- Apple AirPlay & HomeKit
- Accessibility

**Network Settings:**


**Viewing network status:**

1. **Settings → Network**
2. **See:**
    - Connection type (Wireless or Wired)
    - Status (Connected or Not connected)
    - Signal strength (Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor)
    - Download speed
    - IP address

**If connection is "Fair" or "Poor":**

- Move Roku closer to router
- Use WiFi extender
- Switch to Ethernet (if Roku Ultra)
- Improve router placement

**Changing WiFi network:**

1. **Settings → Network → Set up connection → Wireless**
2. **Choose new network**
3. **Enter password**
4. **Connect**

**Useful if:**

- Changed WiFi password
- Got new router
- Moving Roku to different location

**Display Settings:**


**Optimizing picture quality:**


**Display type:**

1. **Settings → Display type**
2. **Options:**
    - Auto-detect (recommended)
    - 720p HD
    - 1080p HD
    - 4K UHD
3. **Choose highest your TV supports**
    - If 4K TV: Select 4K UHD
    - If 1080p TV: Select 1080p HD
    - **Auto-detect usually works perfectly**

**Why it matters:**

- Ensures best picture quality
- Prevents compatibility issues
- 4K content looks best on 4K setting

**HDR (if 4K Roku and 4K HDR TV):**

- **Settings → Display type → 4K TV**
- **HDR mode:** Auto-detect (recommended)
- **Enables HDR** when content supports it

**Adjusting screen refresh rate:**

1. **Settings → Advanced display settings**
2. **Auto-adjust display refresh rate:** Enable
3. **Matches content frame rate** (smoother playback for movies)

**Audio Settings:**


**Optimizing sound:**


**Audio mode:**

1. **Settings → Audio → Audio mode**
2. **Options:**
    - **Stereo:** Standard audio (most TVs)
    - **Dolby Digital:** Surround sound (if you have soundbar/receiver)
    - **DTS:** Surround sound format
    - **Auto:** Roku detects and switches
3. **Select based on your setup**

**If using TV speakers: StereoIf using soundbar with HDMI ARC: Auto or Dolby Digital**


**Volume mode:**

1. **Settings → Audio → Volume mode**
2. **Options:**
    - **Off:** Normal volume
    - **Leveling:** Reduces volume differences (quieter explosions, louder dialogue)
    - **Night:** Compresses dynamic range (great for late-night watching)
3. **Night mode helpful** if you watch with low volume

**Audio output:**

- **HDMI:** Audio through TV or soundbar via HDMI
- **Optical (if available):** Some Roku models support optical audio out

**Subtitle/Closed Caption Settings:**


**Customizing caption appearance:**

1. **Settings → Captions**
2. **Captions mode:**
    - **Off:** No captions
    - **On always:** Always show captions
    - **On replay:** Show when rewinding
    - **On mute:** Show when TV is muted
    - **Custom:** Set per channel
3. **Caption style:**
    - **Text style:** Font, size, color
    - **Background:** Opaque, semi-transparent, transparent
    - **Window:** Caption box appearance
    - **Edge:** Outline, drop shadow, none

**Recommended for readability:**

- Large text
- White text on black background
- Drop shadow or outline

**Captions settings here are default** - individual channels may override


**Theme Settings:**


**Customizing Roku's appearance:**

1. **Settings → Theme**
2. **Choose theme:**
    - Variety of color schemes
    - Different backgrounds
    - Seasonal themes
3. **Preview theme** before applying
4. **Select theme** you like

**Cosmetic only** - doesn't affect functionality


**Screensaver Settings:**


**What happens when Roku is idle:**

1. **Settings → Screensaver**
2. **Change screensaver:** Choose from options
    - Photo slideshow
    - Clock
    - Roku-branded screensavers
    - Download more from Channel Store
3. **Wait time:**
    - How long until screensaver activates
    - 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 minutes, Never
4. **Set based on preference**

**Screensaver prevents TV screen burn-in** (especially important for OLED TVs)


**System Settings:**


**Important system options:**


**Time:**

- **Settings → System → Time**
- **Set time zone**
- **Time format** (12-hour or 24-hour)

**Language:**

- **Settings → System → Language**
- **Change interface language**
- English, Spanish, French, etc.

**Power:**

- **Settings → System → Power**
- **Auto power savings:** Turn off Roku when not in use
- **Screensaver start time**
- **Helpful for energy efficiency**

**System restart:**

- **Settings → System → System restart**
- **Restarts Roku** (fixes many glitches)
- Use this **instead of unplugging**

**System update:**

- **Settings → System → System update**
- **Check now:** Manually check for updates
- **Roku normally auto-updates**, but can force check

**Factory reset:**

- **Settings → System → Advanced system settings → Factory reset**
- **DELETES EVERYTHING** (all channels, settings, account)
- **Use only as last resort** for major problems
- **Requires re-setup from scratch**

**Remote & Device Settings:**


**Managing remotes:**

1. **Settings → Remotes & devices → Remotes**
2. **See paired remotes**
3. **Options:**
    - **Add new remote** (if you bought replacement)
    - **Set up remote for TV control** (program volume/power)
    - **About:** Check remote battery level (enhanced remotes)

**Setup for TV control (if not done during initial setup):**

- **Remotes → Set up remote for TV control**
- **Follow prompts** to program remote for your TV brand

**Privacy Settings:**


**Managing data collection:**

1. **Settings → Privacy**
2. **Smart TV experience:**
    - **Disable** to limit data collection
    - Roku tracks what you watch for recommendations and ads
3. **Advertising:**
    - **Limit ad tracking:** Enable
    - **Reset advertising identifier:** Clears ad profile
4. **Microphone:**
    - **Enable/disable** voice search microphone

**Trade-off:** Better privacy vs personalized experience


**Most people leave defaults**, but privacy-conscious users can tighten these


**Apple AirPlay & HomeKit:**


**If you use Apple devices:**

1. **Settings → Apple AirPlay & HomeKit**
2. **Enable AirPlay:**
    - **Allows iPhone/iPad/Mac** to cast to Roku
    - Screen mirroring from Apple devices
    - Play media from Apple devices
3. **Require code:** Every time or First time only
4. **HomeKit:**
    - Add Roku to Apple Home app
    - Control Roku with Siri
    - "Hey Siri, play Stranger Things on Roku"

**Accessibility Settings:**


**For users with disabilities:**

1. **Settings → Accessibility**
2. **Options:**
    - **Audio guide:** Reads menus and options aloud (for visually impaired)
    - **Captions mode:** Always on
    - **Video description:** Narration of visual elements (when available in content)
    - **Closed captions:** Customization
    - **Speech rate:** How fast audio guide speaks

**Enable features as needed** for easier use


**Optimized Settings Recommendations:**


**For most users:**


`Display type: Auto-detect
HDR: Auto (if 4K TV)
Audio mode: Auto
Volume mode: Leveling or Night
Screensaver: 15 minutes
Captions: On mute or On always
Auto power savings: Enabled
Limit ad tracking: Enabled`


**For 4K TV owners:**


`Display type: 4K UHD
HDR: HDR10/Dolby Vision (check content)
Audio mode: Dolby Digital (if soundbar)
Auto-adjust refresh rate: Enabled`


**For privacy-focused users:**


`Smart TV experience: Disabled
Limit ad tracking: Enabled
Reset advertising identifier: Periodically
Microphone: Disabled (if not using voice)`


**PIN Protection for Purchases:**


**Prevent unauthorized purchases:**

1. **Settings → System → Parental controls**
2. **Create 4-digit PIN**
3. **Require PIN for:**
    - All purchases
    - Adding channels
    - Specific content ratings (PG-13, R, TV-MA)
4. **Save**

**Now purchases require PIN entry** (helpful if kids use Roku or prevent accidental purchases)


**Checking Software Version:**


**Current Roku software:**

1. **Settings → System → About**
2. **See:**
    - Roku model
    - Software version
    - Serial number
    - Device ID
3. **Useful for troubleshooting** and checking if you have latest updates

**Developer Mode (Advanced Users Only):**


**For app development:**

- **Settings → System → Advanced system settings → Enable installer**
- Allows sideloading custom channels
- **Not needed for normal users**
- Can introduce security risks

**The Night Mode Miracle:** If you watch TV late at night and constantly adjust volume (action scenes too loud, dialogue too quiet), enable Night Mode in audio settings. This compresses the dynamic range—explosions get quieter, whispers get louder, and you can keep volume at one consistent level. It's a game-changer for late-night viewing. Similarly, if different channels have wildly different volumes (switch from Netflix to The Roku Channel and get blasted), enable Volume Leveling to even this out.


## Step 7: Troubleshooting Common Problems


When things go wrong, here's how to fix them.


**Problem 1: Roku Won't Turn On / No Power**


**Check:**

- [ ] **Power cable connected?** (Check both ends - Roku and wall/TV USB)
- [ ] **Outlet working?** (Test with another device or try different outlet)
- [ ] **TV USB port providing power?** (Some don't—plug into wall instead)
- [ ] **Status light on Roku?** (Should see light when powered—if no light, no power)

**Solutions:**

1. **Try different outlet** (wall outlet, not power strip)
2. **Use included power adapter** (don't use random USB adapter—may not provide enough power)
3. **Try different USB cable** (if available)
4. **Reset Roku** (see restart instructions below)

**If still no power:** Hardware failure, contact Roku support or replace device


**Problem 2: No Picture on TV / "No Signal"**


**Check:**

- [ ] **TV on correct input?** (Press Input/Source button, cycle through HDMI ports)
- [ ] **HDMI cable firmly connected?** (Both ends—TV and Roku)
- [ ] **Roku powered on?** (Check status light)

**Solutions:**

1. **Verify HDMI input:** Try every HDMI option on TV
2. **Try different HDMI port** on TV
3. **Try different HDMI cable** (if available)
4. **For Streaming Stick:** Use HDMI extender (included) to move stick away from TV
5. **Test HDMI port:** Connect different device to same port (cable box, game console) to verify port works

**Advanced:**

- **Reset display type:** Settings → System → Advanced display settings → Reset display type (Roku cycles through resolutions automatically)

**Problem 3: Roku Won't Connect to WiFi**


**Check:**

- [ ] **Router powered on?** (Lights active)
- [ ] **Other devices connect to WiFi?** (Test with phone—if phone can't connect, router issue not Roku)
- [ ] **Correct WiFi password?** (Double-check every character)
- [ ] **Signal strength?** (Roku should be within 30 feet of router ideally)

**Solutions:**


**Step 1: Restart router**

1. **Unplug router** from power
2. **Wait 30 seconds**
3. **Plug back in**
4. **Wait 2 minutes** for full boot
5. **Try connecting Roku again**

**Step 2: Restart Roku**

1. **Settings → System → System restart**
2. **Or unplug Roku, wait 10 seconds, plug back in**

**Step 3: Forget and reconnect to network**

1. **Settings → Network → Forget network** (if connected)
2. **Set up connection → Wireless**
3. **Select network**
4. **Re-enter password carefully**

**Step 4: Check network settings**

- **Some routers block devices** (MAC address filtering)
- **Check router admin page** (usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1)
- **Add Roku's MAC address** to allowed devices
- **MAC address:** Settings → Network → About

**Step 5: Try different WiFi band**

- **2.4 GHz:** Better range, slower speed
- **5 GHz:** Shorter range, faster speed
- **Some Rokus only see 2.4 GHz**
- **Check router broadcasts both**, enable 2.4 GHz if disabled

**If WiFi still won't work:** Use Ethernet cable (Roku Ultra) or position Roku closer to router


**Problem 4: Buffering / Constant Loading / Poor Quality**


**Causes:** Slow internet or weak WiFi signal


**Check:**

1. **Run speed test** on another device
    - Go to speedtest.net
    - Check download speed
    - **Need:** 3 Mbps for SD, 25 Mbps for HD, 50 Mbps for 4K
2. **Check WiFi signal strength:** Settings → Network → Signal strength
    - **Excellent/Good:** Fine
    - **Fair/Poor:** Improve connection

**Solutions:**


**Improve internet speed:**

- **Close other apps/devices** using internet (pause downloads, close streaming on other devices)
- **Contact ISP** if speeds consistently below plan (upgrade plan if needed)

**Improve WiFi signal:**

- **Move Roku closer to router**
- **Move router higher** (on shelf, not floor)
- **Reduce obstacles** (walls, furniture between router and Roku)
- **Use 5 GHz WiFi** if close to router (faster)
- **Use 2.4 GHz WiFi** if far from router (better range)
- **WiFi extender** or **mesh system** (eero, Google WiFi) for large homes
- **Switch to Ethernet** (Roku Ultra—most reliable)

**Adjust video quality:**

- **Settings → Display type:** Lower from 4K to 1080p
- **Or let content adjust:** Most channels auto-adjust quality based on connection

**Problem 5: Remote Not Working**


**Check:**

- [ ] **Batteries installed correctly?** (Check + and - alignment)
- [ ] **Batteries fresh?** (Replace if old)
- [ ] **Line of sight?** (IR remotes need clear view to Roku)

**Solutions:**


**For all remotes:**

1. **Replace batteries**
2. **For IR remote:** Point directly at Roku (no obstacles)
3. **Restart Roku**

**For WiFi remotes (not responding):**

1. **Re-pair remote:**
    - **Remove batteries** from remote
    - **Unplug Roku** for 5 seconds
    - **Plug Roku back in**, wait for home screen
    - **Reinsert batteries** in remote
    - **Press pairing button** (if present) or **wait 30 seconds** for auto-pairing
    - **Light flashes** on remote during pairing

**Lost remote entirely:**

- **Use Roku mobile app** as remote (temporary or permanent solution)
- **Order replacement remote** from Roku ($20-30)
- **Buy universal remote** that supports Roku

**Problem 6: Apps/Channels Keep Crashing**


**Solutions:**


**Step 1: Close and reopen channel**

- **Press Home button**
- **Reopen channel**

**Step 2: Update channel**

- **Highlight channel**
- **Press ✱ (Star)**
- **Check for updates**
- **Update if available**

**Step 3: Remove and reinstall channel**

1. **Highlight channel**
2. **Press ✱ (Star)**
3. **Remove channel**
4. **Restart Roku:** Settings → System → System restart
5. **Re-add channel** from Channel Store
6. **Sign in again**

**Step 4: Update Roku software**

- **Settings → System → System update → Check now**

**Step 5: Contact channel provider**

- Issue may be with channel's service (Netflix outage, Hulu server issue)
- Check downdetector.com for service status

**Problem 7: Sound But No Picture (or Vice Versa)**


**No picture, but sound:**

- **HDMI cable issue:** Replace HDMI cable
- **Display settings:** Settings → Display type → Reset display type
- **Try different HDMI port** on TV

**Picture but no sound:**

- **Check TV volume** (not muted, volume up)
- **Audio settings:** Settings → Audio → Audio mode → Change to Stereo
- **Check if audio going to soundbar instead of TV** (if you have external speakers)
- **Try different HDMI port**

**HDMI carries both video and audio** - cable issue affects both


**Problem 8: Roku Overheating / Shutting Off**


**Symptoms:** Roku restarts randomly, warning message about overheating


**Causes:**

- Poor ventilation
- Roku in enclosed cabinet
- Streaming Stick against hot TV

**Solutions:**

1. **Improve airflow:**
    - Remove from enclosed space
    - Don't stack devices on top
    - Ensure vents clear
2. **For Streaming Stick:**
    - **Use HDMI extender** (included) to move stick away from heat of TV
    - Cooler position = less overheating
3. **Lower room temperature** (if very hot environment)

**If continues:** Hardware issue, contact Roku support


**Problem 9: Can't Add/Subscribe to Channels**


**Error during channel installation or subscription:**


**Solutions:**

1. **Verify payment method** valid:
    - Go to roku.com → My Account → Payment method
    - Update if expired
2. **Check account status:** Sign in at roku.com
3. **Restart Roku:** Settings → System → System restart
4. **Try adding from computer:** channelstore.roku.com
5. **Contact Roku support** if persists

**Problem 10: Purchased Content Not Appearing**


**Rented or bought movie/show doesn't show up:**


**Solutions:**

1. **Check purchase history:** roku.com → My Account → Purchase history
2. **Verify purchase completed** (got confirmation email)
3. **Look in correct channel's library:**
    - Amazon purchases → Amazon channel
    - Vudu purchases → Vudu channel
    - Roku purchases → The Roku Channel
4. **Sign into channel** with correct account
5. **Restart Roku**
6. **Contact channel support** for refund if charged but no content

**The Universal Fix: Full Restart**


**For most issues, try this first:**


**Method 1: Settings restart (preferred)**

1. **Settings → System → System restart**
2. **Confirm restart**
3. **Wait for Roku to reboot** (30-60 seconds)

**Method 2: Power cycle**

1. **Unplug Roku** from power
2. **Wait 10 seconds**
3. **Plug back in**
4. **Wait for home screen**

**Restarts fix:**

- Frozen screens
- Laggy performance
- Connection issues
- Crashes
- Random glitches

**Always try restart before complex troubleshooting**


**Factory Reset (Last Resort):**


**ONLY if all else fails:**

1. **Settings → System → Advanced system settings → Factory reset**
2. **Enter code displayed** on screen (confirms you want to reset)
3. **Roku erases everything:**
    - All channels
    - All settings
    - Account removed
    - Like new out of box
4. **Must re-setup** from scratch

**OR physical reset:**

- **Locate reset button** on Roku device (small pinhole)
- **Press and hold** with paperclip for 10 seconds
- **Roku resets**

**Use factory reset for:**

- Selling/giving away Roku
- Persistent software issues
- Starting completely fresh

**Checking for Service Outages:**


**If channel not working, might be service outage:**

1. **Visit downdetector.com**
2. **Search for service** (Netflix, Hulu, etc.)
3. **See if widespread outage**
4. **If yes:** Wait for service to restore
5. **If no:** Issue is your Roku/network

**When to Contact Roku Support:**


**Contact support if:**

- Hardware problems (device won't power on, ports not working)
- Persistent software issues after factory reset
- Billing issues
- Account problems

**How to contact:**

- **Support website:** support.roku.com
- **Phone:** 816-272-8106
- **Live chat:** Through support website
- **Social media:** @RokuSupport on Twitter

**Have ready:**

- Roku model
- Software version (Settings → System → About)
- Serial number
- Description of problem
- Troubleshooting steps already tried

**Roku Warranty:**


**Limited warranty:**

- **1 year** from purchase date
- Covers manufacturing defects
- **Does not cover:** Physical damage, liquid damage, normal wear

**Keep receipt** for warranty claims


**The Restart Religion:** In the tech support world, there's a running joke: "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" It's a joke because it's overused, but it's overused because it works. Roku devices are computers, and computers accumulate temporary glitches, memory leaks, and stuck processes. A restart clears all that and starts fresh. Before spending an hour troubleshooting a problem, spend 30 seconds restarting. Settings → System → System restart. You'll be shocked how often this solves the problem instantly.


## Common Questions Answered


**"Do I need a Roku if I have a Smart TV?"**


**Not required, but often better.** Smart TVs have apps built-in, but Roku offers:

- Faster interface
- More apps/channels
- Regular updates (Smart TV support declines after 3-5 years)
- Universal search across all services
- Easier to replace when outdated ($50 vs $500)

Many people with Smart TVs add Roku for better experience.


**"Can I watch regular TV channels on Roku?"**


**Yes and no:**

- **With antenna:** Some Roku models support over-the-air antenna (free ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX, PBS)
- **Live TV streaming services:** YouTube TV ($73/month), Hulu + Live TV ($77/month), Sling TV ($40+/month)
- **Free live TV:** Pluto TV, The Roku Channel (100+ free live channels)
- **Not supported:** Cable/satellite without separate box

**Roku doesn't replace antenna or cable directly, but streaming services can.**


**"How much does Roku cost per month?"**


**Roku itself: $0/month.** Device is one-time purchase.


**Content costs vary:**

- Free channels: $0
- Netflix: $7-23/month
- Hulu: $8-18/month
- Disney+: $8-14/month
- Live TV services: $40-77/month

**You control monthly cost** by choosing which services to subscribe to.


**"Can I use Roku without internet?"**


**No.** Roku requires internet to stream content. No internet = no functionality.


**Exception:** Roku TVs can still function as regular TVs (with antenna/cable box input) without internet.


**"Why do I need a credit card if it's free?"**


**Roku requires payment method** for:

- One-click purchases/rentals
- Subscribing to services through Roku
- Free trials that convert to paid

**You won't be charged unless you make purchases.**


**Workaround:** Use prepaid Visa gift card if you don't want to use real credit card.


**"Can I use Roku in multiple rooms?"**


**Yes.** Buy multiple Roku devices, one per TV.


**Same account:**

- Sign into same Roku account on all devices
- Channels sync across devices

**Cost:** $30-100 per additional Roku


**"Does Roku work with Alexa or Google Assistant?"**


**Yes.**

- **Alexa:** "Alexa, open Netflix on Roku" (requires setup)
- **Google:** "Hey Google, play Stranger Things on Roku"
- **Setup:** Link Roku account in Alexa/Google app

**Also:** Some Roku remotes have voice search built-in (no Alexa/Google needed)


**"Can I record shows with Roku?"**


**Not directly.** Roku doesn't have DVR.


**Options:**

- **Live TV services with cloud DVR:** YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV (record shows to cloud)
- **Separate DVR device:** Tablo (works with antenna, records to hard drive)

**Most streaming is on-demand anyway** (no need to record).


**"What's the difference between Roku stick and Roku box?"**


**Stick:**

- USB size, plugs directly into TV
- Hidden behind TV
- WiFi only
- Cheaper
- Good performance

**Box:**

- Separate device, sits on TV stand
- More powerful (usually)
- May have Ethernet port (Roku Ultra)
- More expensive
- Better for power users

**For most people, stick is fine. Ultra is for enthusiasts.**


**"Can multiple people use Roku at same time?"**


**One Roku = one TV** (one stream at a time on that device)


**But:** Multiple Rokus on same account can stream simultaneously (subject to channel limits - Netflix allows 2-4 streams, Hulu allows 2, etc.)


**"Can I connect Roku to WiFi without password?"**


**No.** Need WiFi password to connect to secured networks.


**If you don't have password:**

- Check router (usually sticker on bottom)
- Contact person who set up internet
- Or use Ethernet cable (Roku Ultra only)

**"Is Roku better than Fire Stick or Apple TV?"**


**Comparison:**


**Roku:**

- Neutral (doesn't favor any service)
- Most channels/apps
- Simple interface
- $30-100

**Fire Stick:**

- Amazon-focused
- Good for Prime members
- Alexa integration
- $30-50

**Apple TV:**

- Premium experience
- Best for Apple ecosystem
- Expensive
- $130-180

**Roku is best for most people** (neutral, affordable, complete). Fire Stick for Amazon users, Apple TV for Apple enthusiasts.


**"Why are there ads on my Roku home screen?"**


**Business model:** Roku makes money from ads (keeps device prices low).


**Can't remove ads**, but can:

- Ignore them
- Accept as trade-off for affordable device
- Use Roku anyway (ads don't affect streaming quality)

**"Can I browse the internet on Roku?"**


**Not really.** Some channels have basic web browsers, but:

- Very limited
- Clunky to use
- Not recommended

**Use computer, phone, or tablet for web browsing.**
